name: General SaaS
description: The cross-cutting product layer every B2B SaaS application needs on top of its vertical features: tenancy and workspaces, onboarding, plans and entitlements, usage metering, team invites, API keys, webhooks, an internal admin console, status/changelog communication, enterprise SSO/SCIM, data export, and feature flags.

sources.title: BoxyHQ SaaS Starter Kit
sources.notes: Verified from repo LICENSE file (Apache-2.0) by an earlier session. Prisma schema: Team (tenant), TeamMember, Invitation, ApiKey, Subscription/Price/Service (billing). Webhooks via svix (pages/api/teams/[slug]/webhooks), SSO via BoxyHQ Jackson SAML (lib/jackson, pages/api/teams/[slug]/sso.ts), SCIM directory sync via Jackson dsync (pages/api/scim/v2.0/[...directory].ts), audit log via Retraced (lib/retraced.ts). No onboarding wizard, no platform-wide admin console/impersonation, no rate limiting found in this repo (checked by grep).

sources.title: NextCRM
sources.notes: Cited here only for its ApiKeys model (prisma model ApiKeys: scope, provider, encryptedKey, per-user) as a second, independent API-key-management implementation. NextCRM is single-tenant (no Team/workspace model) so it does not inform tenancy/invite features.

sources.title: Unleash
sources.notes: Verified license from repo LICENSE file (AGPL-3.0, not Apache as sometimes assumed) via `gh api`; reference-only, never copy code. Inspected src/lib/types/model.ts remotely: FeatureToggle, IFeatureStrategy (strategies+constraints), IEnvironment, IProject, IVariant — feature-flag data model.

sources.title: Lago (billing API)
sources.notes: Verified license from repo LICENSE file (AGPL-3.0) via `gh api`; reference-only, never copy code. Inspected app/models remotely: BillableMetric, Event, DailyUsage, Plan, Entitlement, Wallet, UsageThreshold — usage-metering and plan-entitlement data model.

sources.title: Cachet
sources.license: Custom (Cachet License, source-available, non-OSI, see LICENSE.md)
sources.notes: Custom non-OSI license verified from LICENSE.md via `gh api` (GitHub reports NOASSERTION); reference-only, never copy code. Used only as a single reasoned reference for the shape of a public status/incident page (components, incidents, subscribers). Not independently cross-referenced against a second status-page implementation, so status_page confidence is capped at low-medium.

features.name: Workspace management
features.description: Create, rename, and switch between tenant workspaces; manage workspace-level settings and branding.

provenance.notes: One clear implementation (boxyhq Team model + settings routes); the concept itself is near-universal in B2B SaaS but only one source was directly verified this pass.

features.name: Guided onboarding
features.description: A first-run setup wizard that walks a new workspace owner through initial configuration after signup.

provenance.notes: No dedicated onboarding-wizard code found in boxyhq-saas-starter (checked by grep); this is a reasoned inference from very common B2B SaaS practice (Slack/Notion/Linear-style first-run flows), anchored only to the workspace-creation step that boxyhq does implement. Stated explicitly as low confidence, not industry standard.

features.name: Team invites
features.description: Invite people to a workspace by email with a pre-assigned role; manage pending, accepted, and expired invitations.

provenance.notes: Verified implementation: boxyhq Invitation prisma model + pages/api/teams/[slug]/invitations.ts. Depends on shared.users (generic invite/activation) for the underlying account mechanics; this feature is the workspace-scoped, role-assigning specialization of it.

features.name: Plans and entitlements
features.description: Subscription plan tiers with feature gating and usage/seat limits enforced per workspace.

provenance.notes: boxyhq: Subscription/Price/Service prisma models (Stripe-backed plan tiers). Lago (reference-only, AGPL): explicit Plan + Entitlement + Wallet models. Two independent implementations = medium.

features.name: Usage metering
features.description: Record usage events (API calls, seats, storage, etc.) per workspace to drive limits, alerts, and usage-based billing.

provenance.notes: Single verified implementation (Lago's BillableMetric/Event/DailyUsage models, reference-only). Not found in boxyhq. Common pattern in metered-billing SaaS but only one source cross-referenced this pass.

features.name: API keys
features.description: Issue and revoke scoped API keys per workspace for programmatic access, with prefix display and last-used tracking.

provenance.notes: boxyhq: ApiKey prisma model scoped to a Team, with routes under pages/api/teams/[slug]/. NextCRM: separate ApiKeys model (per-user, per-provider) — a different flavor (storing third-party keys vs issuing the product's own keys) but the same underlying entity/feature shape. Two independent implementations = medium.

features.name: Outbound webhooks
features.description: Let a workspace subscribe to product events and receive signed HTTP callbacks, with delivery retry and a delivery log.

provenance.notes: Single verified implementation: boxyhq's team-scoped webhook endpoints backed by Svix (lib/svix.ts, pages/api/teams/[slug]/webhooks/). Outbound webhooks are near-ubiquitous in API-first SaaS but only one source verified this pass.

features.name: Internal admin console
features.description: An internal, staff-only console for searching tenants, viewing account health, and taking support actions across workspaces.

provenance.notes: No permissively-licensed OSS reference implementation of a platform-wide internal admin console was found in this research pass (boxyhq only has per-tenant admin, not a vendor-side console). Included as a reasoned inference: SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria (CC6/CC7 access-control and monitoring criteria) commonly motivate building one. Confidence intentionally low; do not treat as a directly-sourced feature.

features.name: Public status page
features.description: A public page showing current system status, component health, and incident history, with subscriber notifications.

provenance.notes: Single reference source (Cachet, custom non-OSI license, reference-only) informed the incident/component/subscriber shape. Not cross-referenced against a second implementation this pass.

features.name: Public changelog
features.description: A public or in-app feed of shipped changes and release notes, often paired with an unread-updates indicator.

provenance.notes: No changelog feature found in the sources inspected this pass; included purely as a reasoned inference from common SaaS practice. Anchored to boxyhq only as the domain's general implementation reference, not as direct evidence of this specific feature — confidence deliberately low.

features.name: SSO (SAML)
features.description: Enterprise single sign-on into a workspace via SAML 2.0 against the customer's identity provider.

provenance.notes: Implementation (boxyhq's BoxyHQ Jackson SAML integration, lib/jackson) plus the authoritative SAML 2.0 Core spec together satisfy the brief's high-confidence rule (authoritative source present).

features.name: SCIM provisioning
features.description: Automatic user provisioning and deprovisioning into a workspace from the customer's identity provider via SCIM.

provenance.notes: Implementation (boxyhq Jackson dsync + pages/api/scim/v2.0/[...directory].ts) plus the authoritative SCIM RFC 7643/7644 = high confidence per the brief's rule.

features.name: Self-serve data export
features.description: Let a workspace owner export their tenant's data (CSV/JSON) for backup or portability.

provenance.notes: No direct OSS implementation of self-serve export was found in the sources inspected; GDPR Article 20 (right to data portability) and CCPA's right-to-know/portability provisions are the authoritative motivation. Medium rather than high because the specific self-serve-export *feature shape* is our inference from the regulation, not a spec the regulation defines.

features.name: Feature flags
features.description: Toggle features on/off or roll them out gradually, targeted by workspace, user segment, or environment.

provenance.notes: Single verified implementation (Unleash FeatureToggle/Strategy/Environment/Project model, reference-only, AGPL-3.0). Widely used pattern but only one source cross-referenced this pass.

features.name: Audit log viewer
features.description: A workspace-scoped UI over the audit log with filters, search, and export, for admins to review who changed what.

provenance.notes: Single verified implementation: boxyhq integrates Retraced (lib/retraced.ts) for team-scoped audit history. Depends on shared.audit_log for the underlying append-only record; this feature is the workspace-facing viewer on top of it.

features.name: Self-serve billing portal
features.description: Let a workspace owner view invoices, update payment method, and upgrade/downgrade/cancel their subscription.

provenance.notes: Verified implementation: boxyhq's Stripe-backed Subscription/Price models and webhook handler (pages/api/webhooks/stripe.ts) including subscription status transitions (trialing/active/past_due/canceled). One direct implementation plus this being the de facto standard shape of Stripe Billing Portal integrations.

features.name: Seat management
features.description: Track seats included in a plan, assign/reclaim seats as members are invited or removed, and show pending vs active seat counts.

provenance.notes: boxyhq ties TeamMember to a per-team Subscription; Lago models per-subscription usage/quantity that maps to seat-style metering. Two independent, if partial, sources = medium.

features.name: Custom roles
features.description: Let a workspace define its own roles and permission sets beyond the built-in owner/admin/member roles.

provenance.notes: boxyhq ships only fixed ADMIN/MEMBER roles (lib/permissions.ts) with no custom-role support; this feature is a reasoned inference from common enterprise-tier SaaS practice, anchored to boxyhq's fixed-role model as the contrasting baseline. Confidence deliberately low.

features.name: Trial management
features.description: Time-boxed free trial on a paid plan with expiration handling and trial-to-paid conversion prompts.

provenance.notes: boxyhq's Stripe webhook handler comments enumerate the 'trialing' subscription status, confirming trial support at the billing-provider level, but there is no dedicated trial-management UI/logic in the repo. Single, partial source — low confidence.

features.name: Workspace deletion with export
features.description: Let a workspace owner delete their workspace, with a data export offer and a grace period before hard deletion, supporting the right to erasure.

provenance.notes: boxyhq implements a DELETE team endpoint (pages/api/teams/[slug]/index.ts); GDPR Article 17 (right to erasure) and CCPA deletion rights are the authoritative motivation for the export-then-purge shape. One implementation + one authoritative source = medium (the implementation alone does not confirm the export-before-purge grace period, which is our inference).

features.name: Public API rate limiting
features.description: Per-key and per-plan request rate limits on the public API, with standard rate-limit response headers.

provenance.notes: No rate-limiting middleware found in boxyhq-saas-starter (checked by grep); reasoned inference from standard public-API practice, anchored to the same API-key entity boxyhq does implement. Confidence deliberately low.

features.name: Sandbox / test environment
features.description: A separate test workspace or API mode with synthetic data, isolated from production, for integration testing.

provenance.notes: Not found in any source inspected this pass; reasoned inference from common developer-tool SaaS practice (e.g. payment-provider test modes), anchored to boxyhq's API-key entity as the mechanism a sandbox key would use. Confidence deliberately low.

features.name: Data residency controls
features.description: Let an enterprise workspace pin where its data is stored/processed (e.g. EU vs US region) to satisfy jurisdictional requirements.

provenance.notes: Not found as a concrete feature in any source inspected; reasoned inference motivated by GDPR cross-border transfer rules and ISO/IEC 27001 asset-location controls, which enterprise customers commonly ask about. No implementation evidence, so capped at low despite two authoritative anchors.
